articles.title: Exponential Equations, Explained: The Math Behind the Harvard 3^x = x^9 Question
articles.excerpt: An exponential equation is an equation where the unknown sits in the exponent: 2^x = 32, 5^x = 125, e^x = 20. The equation 3^x = x^9 went viral as a "Harvard question" because it looks impossible and…
articles.body: An exponential equation is an equation where the unknown sits in the exponent: 2^x = 32, 5^x = 125, e^x = 20. The equation 3^x = x^9 went viral as a "Harvard question" because it looks impossible and then resolves into a 13-digit exact match. Here is the math — the general method, the famous answer, and the second solution most explanations skip. The One Idea That Solves a^x = b Logarithms undo exponents. That is the whole method. Take the natural log of both sides of a^x = b: ln(a^x) = ln(b) Apply the power rule, ln(a^x) = x · ln(a): x · ln(a) = ln(b) Divide by ln(a): x = ln(b) / ln(a) That single formula solves every equation of the form a^x = b (for a > 0, a ≠ 1, b > 0). Two examples: 2^x = 32 → x = ln 32 / ln 2 = 5. Exact, because 32 = 2^5. 2^x = 3 → x = ln 3 / ln 2 ≈ 1.5850.

articles.title: XAUUSD Explained for Price Tracking and Alerts
articles.excerpt: XAUUSD Explained for Price Tracking and Alerts Summary: XAUUSD quotes gold in US dollars per troy ounce. It is useful for following gold prices, building dashboards, and setting price alerts, but the…
articles.body: XAUUSD Explained for Price Tracking and Alerts Summary: XAUUSD quotes gold in US dollars per troy ounce. It is useful for following gold prices, building dashboards, and setting price alerts, but the symbol alone does not identify an executable price or tell you whether to buy or sell. For example, a synthetic bid of 2,400.00 and ask of 2,400.80 produce a midpoint of 2,400.40, but neither that calculation nor a threshold alert guarantees an execution price. XAUUSD is the common market symbol for gold priced in US dollars. A quote of 2,400 would mean 2,400 US dollars per troy ounce of gold; that number is an illustration, not a live price. XAU identifies gold and USD identifies the currency used to express its value.

articles.title: From Spring Boot to EF Core: Understanding Concurrency a Little Differently
articles.excerpt: Coming from Spring Boot to EF Core, I expected version-based concurrency control to work more or less the same way. The goal was familiar: prevent one update from silently overwriting another. But whi…
articles.body: Coming from Spring Boot to EF Core, I expected version-based concurrency control to work more or less the same way. The goal was familiar: prevent one update from silently overwriting another. But while working with SQL Server's rowversion in EF Core, I noticed a small difference that made me rethink what a version column actually represents. What I was used to in Spring Boot When working with JPA/Hibernate, we can use @version to enable optimistic locking. For example: @Entity public class Product { @Id private Long id ; private String name ; @Version private Long version ; } Hibernate manages the version field. When an entity is updated, its version is incremented, and the version is checked during the update.

articles.title: Scraping Flipkart with Python in 2026: skip the CSS, read the page's JSON state
articles.excerpt: Copy the CSS selectors from most Flipkart scraping tutorials and you get nothing back. The ._30jeq3 price class and the ._4rR01T name class match zero cards on today's pages. Build fresh ones and they…
articles.body: Copy the CSS selectors from most Flipkart scraping tutorials and you get nothing back. The ._30jeq3 price class and the ._4rR01T name class match zero cards on today's pages. Build fresh ones and they break by category: a title selector that matches 24 of 24 cards on a laptop search matches 0 of 40 on a shoe search, because Flipkart renders two card layouts with different hashed class names. The surprising part: Flipkart barely blocks anyone. What changes is which page you get. This post walks through three scrapers (search results, product details, reviews) that read the JSON Flipkart already ships with every page, using only requests , json , re and csv .

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

articles.body: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials.
